# Security review

The supplied file src/flask/signals.py only declares blinker signals and contains no exploitable logic. The review is limited to this single file, so any security concerns related to signal receivers, dispatch, or downstream usage cannot be assessed from the provided content.

## Findings

- No concrete security issues were identified in src/flask/signals.py. The file is purely declarative: it instantiates a blinker Namespace and creates named signal objects (template_rendered, request_started, etc.).
- The code contains no input handling, dynamic code execution (eval/exec), SQL queries, file system access, or network operations, so there are no injection, deserialization, or file-related attack surfaces within this file.
- Signal names are string literals, not derived from user input, so there is no risk of signal-name injection or namespace pollution from untrusted data.
- The blinker Namespace and Signal objects are standard, well-established primitives; the security posture depends on how receivers are registered and invoked elsewhere, which is outside the scope of this single-file review.
